#768. Smith: I want to play on the PGA Tour

Cameron Smith joined LIV Golf in 2022 after clinching his first major at The Open at St Andrews; the Australian will play select events on the DP World Tour in 2027; watch Smith in action at this week's BMW Australian PGA Championship live on Sky Sports

Cameron Smith has moved on from LIV Golf, is preparing for his invitation-only appearances on the DP World Tour and is already thinking about a return to the PGA Tour.

As the 2022 British Open champion prepared for the BMW Australian PGA Championship starting Thursday at The Lakes in Sydney, attention inevitably turned to his career goals and his steps toward a possible return to the PGA Tour.

"I guess that's the path. That's where I want to be now for sure," Smith told the Australian Associated Press.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"DP's given us a chance to kind of fulfil that. We'll see how that goes. There's plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it's going to be difficult.

"But for sure that's where I want to play."

Smith will not return as a full-time member on the DP World Tour, but is one of a number of former LIV players, including Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson, to sign an agreement with the tour to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments during the 2027 season, excluding Rolex Series events.

He receives an exemption to play this week, having won the BMW Australian PGA Championship three times in 2017, 2018 and 2022.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Under the DP World Tour and PGA Tour's current agreement, the top 10 players on the Race to Dubai Rankings qualify for the PGA Tour.

The number of PGA Tour cards available to players finishing at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings for the 2028 season is yet to be determined, with the PGA Tour set to launch its new two-tier championship structure the year after next.

However, to even have a chance at winning one of those coveted cards, Smith will need to play more tournaments on the DP World Tour's 2027 schedule.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

He could do that by winning the co-sanctioned BMW Australian PGA Championship or the Australian Open at Kingston Heath, which begins on December 3 and also features Rory McIlroy.

"I think given what they've told me, I pretty much need to win this year to get membership," Smith said.

"It's all still very blurry to me at the moment. There are a lot of rules, but we'll have a few opportunities, and like I said, I've always managed to play pretty good down here, so why not start it off with a good one?"

The PGA Tour board last week said it had "thoughtful discussions" about the future of players at LIV Golf but otherwise seemed to be in no hurry to decide if there is room for them next season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

CEO Brian Rolapp said the Returning Member Program, which allowed Brooks Koepka to return to the PGA Tour at the beginning of 2026 with financial penalties, was not on the table.

Smith didn't take up that one-time offer in January, which applied only to players who'd won majors or The Players Championship from 2022 through 2025, which included himself, Koepka, Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Smith is in a kind of limbo. LIV Golf, which lost the financial support of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and filed for bankruptcy on September 8, told a bankruptcy court earlier this month it had abandoned plans for a new version of the league and had begun winding down its business.

"There was a lot of uncertainty and then in a way it was good to just like get the noise over and done with," Smith, who joined LIV after winning The Open at St Andrews in 2022, said.

"It was a big move to go LIV at the start for sure, and I think everyone that was close to me and all my friends saw why I was doing it and why I made the decision."

Adam Scott said he had no doubts about Smith fitting back in.

"Cam's incredibly talented and he'll adjust to his new environment," Scott said. "He'll be just fine."

#767. Spurs 'a match for anyone' as win at Man City boosts European hopes

Spurs secure famous win as Man City falter again

Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.

The Women's Super League has an established big four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.

But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.

Two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.

They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.

"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho said in his post-match media conference.

"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game."

Man City beaten by Spurs and miss chance to go top of WSL

Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.

They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.

Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.

The big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.

What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.

Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.

Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.

Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.

That was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 â until Tottenham tore up the script.

The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.

Spurs have rediscovered form after losing all three league games in October while conceding 14 goals

Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.

After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.

After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.

Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.

In midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.

"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," said Ho.

"We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass."

Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.

In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.

They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.

It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.

"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent."

City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.

When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.

Vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.

Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.

It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.

Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.

There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

#766. Selena Gomez Reacts to Martin Short, Meryl Streep Romance Rumors

Selena Gomez cheekily reacted to Martin Short bringing up Meryl Streep in a conversation about Only Murders in the Building guest stars, two years after the pair sparked romance rumors.

Selena Gomez just proved you’re not the only one hoping for Meryl Streep and Martin Short romance.

During an Only Murders in the Building FYC event in Hollywood Nov. 19, Gomez cheekily jumped in while Short detailed his awe of working with Streep, as well as Jennifer Saunders and Olivia Coleman.

“I don’t know why Meryl keeps coming up,” Gomez joked to laughs from the audience as well as Short himself. “Finally, I get to reuse a joke. Yes!”

To which Short wiped his eyes adding, “I know.”

Earlier that same day, Gomez had made a similar joke while taping an episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live! alongside Short.

“I get so geeked out,” Gomez admitted of working alongside Streep. “We’ve worked together for a while.”

And when Short—whose wife Nancy Dolman died following a cancer battle in 2010—clarified it was Streep’s fourth season on Only Murders, Gomez quipped, “Yeah, I don’t know why she keeps coming back.”

Visibly taken aback, Short simply added, “Yeah, I don’t know either.”

Of course, romance rumors have been stirring between Short and Streep since 2024, when they appeared to be getting closer after Streep joined the series the year prior, particularly following a cozy night out at the Golden Globes.

But while the pair share an on-screen romance, a rep for Short confirmed to E! News at the time that the pair were “just very good friends” but “nothing more.”

Nevertheless, Short has admitted that even he was starstruck by working with the Devil Wears Prada alum—who announced she split from her husband Don Gummer in 2023.

“The first day of shooting with her, I was going to work, and—you know, I'm not new to show business,” Short told E! News in 2024. “I thought, ‘I am nervous today. Why?' Oh yeah, I'm working with Meryl.”

The Saturday Night Live alum was floored, however, when he learned that Streep felt the same.

"She said, ‘Okay, my nerves are to half,’” he recalled. “I went, ‘Oh, okay, that's pretty cool. Maybe that's why you're the greatest actress, because you've never taken anything for granted.’”

For more stars who never dated despite their on-screen chemistry sparking romance rumors, keep reading…

The Anyone But You costars may have found love onscreen, but that's where it stayed. Despite the onslaught of dating rumors amid their 2023 press tour, the pair emphasized that their relationship was strictly platonic.

"The two things that you have to sell a rom-com are fun and chemistry," Powell told the New York Times in April 2024. "Sydney and I have a ton of fun together, and we have a ton of effortless chemistry. That's people wanting what's on the screen off the screen, and sometimes you just have to lean into it a bit—and it worked wonderfully. Sydney is very smart."

Meanwhile, Sweeney—who was engaged to businessman Jonathan Davino at the time, though they split in March 2025 after seven years together—asserted that she and Powell didn't play up their chemistry ahead of the rom-com's release.

"Honestly, the press did it themselves. There was no leaning in, per se," she told Variety in October 2025. "Truly, the tabloids and journalists just created it and kept going."

"Glen and I genuinely care for each other and have a love and respect for one another," the actress emphasized. "I love being with him. And I think people just truly saw a really beautiful pairing."

Hermione Granger and Draco Malfoy?! If Watson had it her way, the Harry Potter franchise would have had a Hogwarts House-crossed romance going down off-screen. The actress has admitted to nursing a serious crush on her bleached blonde costar.During the Harry Potter 20th anniversary special, Watson shared that as a child she "fell in love" with Felton while on the set of their first film together, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. "I used to come in every day and look for his number on the call sheet, it was No. 7, and if his name was on the call sheet, it was an extra exciting day," she said during the reunion. "He was three years above me and so for him he was like, 'You're like my little sister.'"Shortly after the special premiered, fans of the series quickly took to the Internet to share their wish for the longtime friends to become something more.However, in an interview with British Vogue, Watson addressed the online reaction and put any potential dating rumors to rest. "We speak most weeks," she said, "and we just think it's sweet."

The one where Ross and Rachel were almost each other's lobsters in real-life.During HBO Max's Friends reunion, Aniston and Schwimmer—who played one of TV's most beloved couples—explained that art reflected real life a bit during the show's first season. "At some point, we were both crushing hard on each other, but it was like two ships passing because one of us was always in a relationship, and we never crossed that boundary," Schwimmer said. "We respected that."Aniston added, "Honestly, I remember saying one time to David, 'It's going to be such a bummer if the first time you and I actually kiss is going to be on national television.' And sure enough, the first time we kissed was in that coffee shop."So, instead of having a romance IRL, she explained that they "just channeled all of our adoration and love for each other into Ross and Rachel."

Arguably one of the most iconic pairings in movie history, fans have shipped Leo and Kate together since 1996's Titanic (even though she didn't make room for him on that door). Still, they never let go of their friendship, with Winslet telling The Guardian that they are "bonded for life." From walking the red carpet together at the 1998 Golden Globes to watching DiCaprio blow kisses to Winslet during her emotional 2009 Golden Globes speech, it's so evident that the feelings between the besties have only continued to grow over the past two decades, iceberg be damned.

The unexpected pairing's chemistry in 2019's A Star Is Born and its ensuing press tour made fans blind to the fact that the actor was dating Irina Shayk and the "Bad Romance" singer was engaged to Christian Carano at the time.Still, it was clear that the costars had a close bond, with Gaga revealing that she had an "instant connection" with Cooper that came "the second that I saw him."Of course, that closeness was on full display when the pair took to the Oscars stage in 2019, hand-in-hand, to perform their Best Song-winning number, "Shallow," just days after Gaga ended her engagement.

But the House of Gucci star quickly shut down romance rumors following the performance, telling Jimmy Kimmel, "Yes, people saw love and—guess what—that's what we wanted you to see."Cooper, whose romance with Shayk ended later that year, never addressed the speculation until November 2021, telling The Hollywood Reporter they were acting during the Oscar performance."They kind of fall in love in that scene in the film," he explained. "It's that explosive moment that happens to them on a stage in front of thousands of people…It would have been so weird if we were both on stools facing the audience."

Gaga isn't the first costar Cooper has been romantically linked to in the press, with his onscreen dynamic with Lawrence in movies such as Silver Linings Playbook and American Hustle sparking rumors for years. In fact, Cooper was asked by Howard Stern in 2015, "When are you two gonna have sex? Everyone is waiting for that." The actor was quick to respond, "Never. It's just not the way we are together."And, at the 2013 Golden Globes, when he was asked by Entertainment Tonight if they were were dating, Cooper responded, "Oh my god. That's very funny. No, my God, no."

Since starring in Speed together in 1994, rumors have raced over the decades that Bullock and Reeves had an off-screen romance. Alas, it was never meant to me, with Sandra denying the two were ever a couple in an interview with Esquire magazine."Nope...but who knows?," she said. "Keanu's a guy who, I feel like, is friends with every woman he's ever dated. I don't think there's anyone who has something horrible to say about him. So maybe we could have survived. I don't know. But we didn't have to survive anything. We just get to grow up together on parallel roads and tip our hats and meet for a dinner and try to work together. And the longer time goes on, the more in awe I am of the human being. Would I have been able to say that if he had dumped me and made me angry? Probably not."Still, the duo, who also costarred in 2006's The Lake House, are close friends, with Bullock citing Reeves's listening skills as one of his best attributes. The Miss Congeniality star recalled that about a year after filming Speed, she casually mentioned to her costar that she'd never had champagne and truffles. A few days later, she told the outlet, Reeves hand-delivered those two items (and flowers), explaining, "I just thought you might want to try champagne and truffles, to see what it's like."

Moviegoers have Crazy, Stupid, Love for this pairing after they've played romantic interests in three films, including La La Land.Though they never dated in real life, working together forged a bond between the two actors. During a Q&A session at the 2018 Telluride Film Festival, the Cruella star revealed how much Gosling meant to her and his impact on her life and career. Calling him a "dear, wonderful friend," Stone said, "I can't even imagine what my life would be without Ryan. She then added, "He's so special. It makes me emotional."And before La La Land debuted in 2016, Stone joked around about the number of films she's done with Gosling, telling E! News, "He has a restraining order against me now.""Restraining order" aside, Gosling said it was "great to work" with Emma, explaining, "I think it brings the best out of [us] because you know one another, and you are able to help each other in a way that you can't if you're strangers."

Jim and Pam on The Office are one of the most beloved TV couples of all-time, with fans rooting for the Dunder Mifflin employees to be together throughout the NBC hit's nine-year run. Jam's chemistry never transitioned into an off-screen romance between John and Jenna, though she did admit to the pair having "real chemistry" during a 2016 appearance on Watch What Happens Live when a caller asked how close they were."There's like a real part of me that is Pam and a real part of him that's Jim and those parts of us were genuinely in love with one another," Fischer explained. "But in real life we aren't totally Pam and totally Jim, so in real life we're not the perfect match…he was like a type of spouse that I had for a long time, he was my partner and we will always be close because of it."Krasinski later weighed in on his costar's headline-making comments, telling The Daily Beast, "I think we both feel it's such an honor to be a part of that relationship. As far as how she was quoted about saying we were 'genuinely in love,' I think that was taken wildly out of context and I feel bad for her."We'll always have the teapot.

They may have costarred in How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, but the pair gained a rapid number of fans rooting for them to find each other IRL after the 2006 rom-com. But it never happened.In an interview with Howard Stern on his SiriusXM show in October 2020, McConaughey revealed it simply never appealed to him to date one of his famous costars."I've always tried to keep it professional and the people I worked with, I must say, did it well," he shared. "Maybe we had certain crushes on each other at certain times but we always just kept it professional."

And with that, the chance for their love to blossom died, just like that love fern.

These A-list best friends have off-the-charts on-screen chemistry (Ocean's Eleven, anyone?) that has extended offscreen in a purely platonic way. Just look at their giggle-filled interviews, gushing public speeches and the fact that George has lent out his coveted Lake Como home to the Roberts-Moder family for anniversary celebrations. NBD!

Along with the ball dropping on New Year's Eve, you can always count on people wondering if the best friends and CNN's Live From Times Square co-hosts have ever dated. When Cohen appeared on Howard Stern's radio show, he was asked, "What is it about Anderson Cooper that keeps you from falling in love with him?" The Watch What Happens Live host replied, "I just think it's not what our relationship is based on. We're just friends. That's not a part of it. I think, at this point, we know each other too well. We're not attracted to each other in that way."Funnily enough, the pair first met when they were set up on a blind date over 25 years ago. "You know when straight people know two gay guys, they're like, 'Oh, you guys should meet,'" Cooper said on The Tonight Show in 2017, adding that when the two had a phone call to schedule the date, he "knew within 45 seconds I was never going on a date with Andy Cohen."He explained that Cohen "violated" a cardinal rule" when it comes to dating the CNN host: He asked about Anderson's mother, Gloria Vanderbilt. "I wanted to date the Vanderbilt boy!" Cohen admitted. "I was excited!"

While Deschanel said the pair had "so much fun" making the 2009 indie rom-com (500) Days of Summer, Gordon-Levitt admitted dating his costar and longtime friend would be "awkward" in a 2012 interview with Playboy."Zooey and I just think it's funny," he said of fans wanting them to be together. "It is funny. We've been friends for 10 years."

Before it was confirmed that the High School Musical heartthrob was dating his costar Vanessa Hudgens, there was speculation that he was involved with their mutual best friend Tisdale. His 2006 guest appearance as her love interest on The Suite Life of Zack and Cody only fueled the rumors.Efron and Tisdale still remain close to this day, with the latter calling him her "brother/best friend," though she did pick him as her worst onscreen kiss in an interview with Elle. "It was the worst because he is like my brother," Tisdale explained. "At the time, he was used to acting on Warner Brothers, which is CW, and we were on Disney Channel."She then called him out for trying to kiss her "with his tongue," prompting her to tell him, "'Get away from me!'""I closed my mouth so fast. I was like, 'This is Disney Channel, we don't kiss like that on Disney Channel!'" Tisdale recalled. "It's just weird when you're so close to somebody, we'd already done a movie, I'd known him for years before,'" she said. "'That is why it was the worst, it's just we're too close.'"

While their High School Musical characters Chad and Taylor were teen sweethearts, Bleu and Coleman left the Disney franchise with a lifelong friendship. The duo reunited onscreen in the 2021 Lifetime Christmas movie, A Christmas Dance Reunion, with Bleu writing on Instagram, "After 13 years it felt like coming home working and dancing with [Monique] again. Starring in a [Lifetime] Christmas movie has always been a dream of mine, but never in a million years did I think I'd get to share the screen with one of my favorite people."And Coleman is hoping to continue working with "one of her best friends," telling People, "I honestly pray that we get to do more things together because we have that sort of spark that Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan had, and Leo and Kate, and Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling, and all of these different couples that we've seen in movie after movie together. I really feel like we have that potential as well and I'd like to see that happen."

They may have played one of TV's most iconic will-they-or-won't-they couples on The X-Files, but the costars actually didn't get along while filming their hit Fox show. In a 2008 interview with Metro UK, Duchovny admitted that he often fought with Anderson during the series' initial eight-year run because, "Familiarity breeds contempt. It's nothing to do with the other person. We used to argue about nothing. We couldn't stand the sight of each other."That didn't stop fans from wanting Mulder and Scully to get together, both on-screen and off, with a photo from their May 2021 lunch date going viral, much to Duchovny's amusement. "As I was leaving she was like, 'Let's take a photo,'" he told People. "I was told there was a big reaction to it! I never get that stuff, but it's really cool that people are interested after all these years."

Avengers shippers, assemble!While they've appeared in nine movies together since first collaborating on 2004's The Perfect Score, the superhero costars have never hooked up IRL. But Evans and Johansson have developed a deep comfort level with each other over the years. "It's really a result of 10 years of knowing somebody," Johansson explained of their chemistry to Entertainment Weekly in March 2020, "and being able to have a kind of intimacy with them that I think you get from just spending a lot of time with somebody and knowing their soft underbelly."

#759. Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?

Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

Young people across Germany and Europe are taking to the streets, voicing fears of a bleak future.

But is that really the case? Does Gen Z face greater challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s? What do the two generations have in common, and where do their experiences differ?

"Of course, it's fair to ask, 'Were things just as tough for you back then?'" youth researcher Simon Schnetzer tells DW. "But young people see that things are difficult for them now, and say that's why they need support today."

Schnetzer, who wrote the annual Youth in Germany study, highlights one key question raised by the recent demonstrations across Europe as: "Have we given young people the conditions they need to live and work here with confidence, and to keep this system funded?"

His straightforward answer is no. A survey of the statistics shows that both Gen Z and the Baby Boomers are affected by major societal changes, but in different ways. DW surveyed data on pensions, education, housing and climate change to find out more.

The facts point to a clear trend: Fewer and fewer young people are having to support an ever-growing number of retirees. According to the Germany's public pension insurance system, there were 3.73 contributors for every retiree in 1957. By 2025, that figure had fallen to just 2.1.

By 2045, this number is projected to drop to just 1.73 contributors per retiree. In absolute terms, this means 35.35 million contributors will be financing pensions for 16.82 million retirees.

To cushion this trend and keep contribution rates stable, the pension system already receives around €118 billion [$131 billion] in annual government subsidies. This amounts to roughly 25% of the federal budget. That means an increasing share of the population will be called upon to help fund pensions.

There are also signs that many people's pensions are already falling short of covering their living expenses. The number of retirees relying on federal basic income support has risen from 257,000 in 2003 to 738,000 in 2024.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Rising rents hit low-income households particularly hard. According to a report by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW), the share of income spent on rent by low-income households rose from around 24% in 1990 to nearly 36% in 2021.

This means that in 2021, the lowest-income households spent an average of 14 percentage points more of their income on rent than high-income households.

According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), in 2025, an average of 11% of the population spent more than 40% of their disposable income on housing costs. Among people at risk of poverty, the figure was as high as 35%.

However, according to calculations by real estate platform Jacasa, Boomers could actually help ease pressure on the housing market in the coming years. They currently own around 4.8 million owner-occupied houses and apartments.

Over the coming decades, these properties are expected to change hands as former occupants sell them, move into assisted living, or hand them down through inheritance. In some regions, this could lead to an oversupply of properties and, consequently, lower prices, according to Jacasa's projections.

According to the federal government's Education Finance Report, public spending on education for people under 30 has doubled since 2011, rising from around €4,000 to approximately €8,000 per person annually.

Despite this increase, Germany ranks only in the middle of the pack internationally. According to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), public education spending accounted for 4.6% of Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022, compared with an OECD average of 4.7%.

However, the additional funding cannot solve the problem of teacher shortages. According to estimates by the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, Germany will be short of around 27,000 teachers by 2035. The main reasons are the wave of Baby Boomer retirements and declining birth rates, which have contributed to a shortage of young teachers.

Back in 1972, the Club of Rome warned of the consequences of global warming in its landmark publication The Limits to Growth. According to the United Nations, the planet is on track for 2.6°C of warming by the end of the century compared with pre-industrial levels.

If the world maintains its current climate policies, children who are six years old today could experience heat waves two to seven times as often as Boomers did over their lifetimes. That was the finding of a 2025 study by Vrije University in Brussels.

The deadly impact of extreme weather is already evident in rising death tolls during recent heatwaves. According to Germany's Robert Koch Institute (RKI), an estimated 16,000 people died from heat-related causes across Germany by mid-September 2026. The vast majority — more than 14,000 — were over the age of 65.

"Gen Z and Baby Boomers are in the same boat. We need to bring them together, because otherwise younger people have no prospects for prosperity, and neither do older generations," youth researcher Schnetzer concludes.

He suggests that both generations take to the streets and protest together, adding that would just be the beginning. "What needs to follow is a constructive process to define goals and measures that everyone can support," he said. "Even if it means making sacrifices."

This article was originally published in German.

#758. Bo Derek Reveals Secret to Decades-Long Romance With John Corbett

Bo Derek shared rare insight into her relationship with husband John Corbett over 20 years into their love story, detailing what still makes them click.

The Bolero actress revealed the secret to making her relationship with husband John Corbett with after over two decades together.

"I fall in love," Derek, 70, told The Hollywood Reporter in an interview published Nov. 20. "I fall hard, and I think that when someone else truly loves you, it’s such a gift to cherish. It’s kind of a miracle with all the billions of people in the world, so I cherish it."

Her comment comes after she provided some rare insight into her life with the Sex and the City actor—whom she wed in 2020 after 18 years of dating—including how he commemorated her recent 70th birthday.

"He’s a great gift giver," Derek told People earlier this month. “I have a friend with a company. He’s very successful, and he’s starting a new company. And John went and got me shares in his company. It’s so much fun. I am not a wheeler dealer or a trader by any means. It’s all just algebra to me."

Ultimately, though, it's Corbett's presence in her life that is the biggest gift of all.

"He keeps me laughing," Derek said. "He’s very youthful, enthusiastic."

While the couple occasionally hosts a couple of friends for small dinner parties at their 110-acre ranch near Santa Barbara, Calif., they tend to prefer spending time at home with one another and their two German Shepherds.

"When we first met, he didn’t want to have a girlfriend with a dog because they just require too much time," Derek shared. "You’re just off going off having fun, and you got to rush back to the dog. And now I can’t get him to go anywhere with me because he doesn’t want to leave the dogs."

Keep reading for more celeb couples who have shared the secrets to their long-lasting relationships...

"I never thought that I would laugh this much in my marriage. That is such a fundamental ingredient of who you are, this insistence on joy," Hermann detailed to his bride of their partnership of over 20 years in Marlo Thomas and Phil Donahue's 2020 book What Makes a Marriage Last. "And I think what sustains our marriage is that I know you love me in spite of who I am, and that is the definition of grace."Seeking out that happiness is key. Even after a particularly robust argument, "One of us will test the waters with a joke—about the very thing we were fighting about," Herman shared of life with the Law & Order: SVU star. "It's like one of us says, 'I'm not saying I was wrong, and I'm not still insisting I was entirely right, but can we at least inch our way back toward the place where we caught at stuff together?' Once that happens, it's a pretty good sign that things are on their way to getting patched up."

They've avoided need for any major renovation by sticking to the same advice they got in premarital counseling ahead of their 2003 vows. Even five kids in, Tuesday date nights are a must and they've held off on purchasing a TV, instead finding other ways to connect. But if Chip were to offer any tip to follow, it'd be to pursue the person you love "like a hornet." Some two decades in, he said, he still feels like the guy hoping to get a second date. "I'm not saying she'd never cheat on me," he explained, "but it's not going to be because I never told her I loved her or because I didn't send her flowers or I forgot our anniversary."

"My first piece of advice is not to take advice from celebrities," Bacon joked of his 36-year union. It's as succinct as their other go-to, "Keep the fights clean and the sex dirty," a phrase developed specifically to end any further chatter about their marriage. Truthfully, though, they make it a point not to let arguments linger, rarely digging in for the sake of the victory. "Honestly, we don't like to fight, so when we actually are in an argument, we're both looking for a solution," The Closer actress explained to Thomas and Donahue. "For the most part we're struggling to get back to everything being okay, because it sucks to fight." Because, when it comes down to it, she continued, "There is no Plan B. No matter what, we want to work it out."

Over 37 years into marriage, the actors have mastered the art of fighting fair. "Tracy and I don't pick scabs," explained the Family Ties alum. "In some marriages, people look at their partner and see vulnerability and they just can't help but go after that vulnerability, like it's a sport or something. We don't do that." That's not to say they don't have arguments. "If I've said something stupid, I have the tendency to want to take it back and make it all okay," he said. "But that doesn't really work." Instead, he follows her lead and tries to give her space. She, in turn, offers up understanding: "Sometimes you just have to say to yourself, 'You know what? He said something schmucky and it made me feel bad. But he's a good person and I'm going to give him the benefit of the doubt that he didn't realize that what he said hurt my feelings.'"

"He still makes me laugh more than any human being," Curtis said about the Waiting for Guffman director on Today in December 2024, ahead of the couple's 40th wedding anniversary, adding jokingly, "and I'm sure there's something about me that he likes. I don't know what it is, but I'm sure there's something."

"I think one of the things that has kept us together all of these years is that we both define relationships as something that's relatively indefinable," the How I Met Your Mother alum said. Through 21 years of career shifts (actor-chef Burtka released his cookbook Life Is a Party in 2019), parenting twins Gideon and Harper and dealing with tough times, "Marriage never stays the same," explained Harris. "When you have sex with the same person over and over, it gets redundant, and so you try different things. Then one day you don't like each other, and suddenly you're not attracted to each other, so you have to figure out how to be reattracted to them—but in a different way because you're aging."Eventually, he continued, you find yourself more attracted to their soul. And then their body again. "It all keeps morphing," he noted. "So in a weird way, we keep falling in love with each other in different ways, over and over."

Appropriately, the comic actors believe their funniness gives them life. And not just in their 19-year union itself. "Whenever we have a good laugh," noted the Can You Ever Forgive Me? actress, "especially a crazy one, when you're like, Oh, my God, and you're almost dizzy—we always assign it a specific amount of time that it added to our lives. And I'm always adding it up. I'll say, 'Okay, that was like two months—I just got two more months to live!'"They put a time limit on disagreements as well. Citing the oft-repeated don't go to bed angry rule, Falcone, said, "I tried it once, and I realized that in the morning I had forgotten what I was mad about. You're not getting any answers if you're parsing out an argument when everybody is tired and possibly had a drink or two. I've never had the thing where you're having an argument at ten o'clock at night, and then you say, 'Well, that was good. I'm glad we got to the bottom of that. We agree. Truce signed.'"

Each having wed before they found their way to the other in 1995, they not only had to navigate a marriage, but life as step-parents to two children apiece. "There is no book that tells you how to do it, so the one thing I figured out right away is that they already have a mom—and it's not me. So what did they need from me?" the Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist actor recalled. "That's when I realized that everybody needs a cheerleader, right? There's never too many of those in your life, so that's what I'll be. I never set their boundaries, disciplined them, or tried to teach them right from wrong. They have parents who do that."The Cheers alum agreed with her stance wholeheartedly. "I think that's really wise, to offer yourself as a friend," he said. "‘I'm not going to discipline you and I'm not going to judge you. What I'm going to do is hang out with you and be there for you.' And that's what you have to do: absolutely, genuinely be there."

The moment same-sex civil unions were legalized in Britain, the music icon and the Canadian ad exec were joined together in a Dec. 21, 2005 ceremony. They repeated the process on the exact same day nine years later once they were able to legally wed. And yet the anniversary they recognize is their unexpected meeting during a 1993 weekend dinner party at the singer's Windsor, England flat, his friend having set the guest list.Every Saturday, no matter where they are in the world, together or apart, the two pen a handwritten note to each other, by the authors' count, some 1,352 letters in all. "There's something very spiritual and real about handwriting," explains Furnish, "and the cards are a chance to reflect on the week that's passed and talk about the week that's coming up." Agreed the five-time Grammy winner, "It's part of the success, I think, of a lasting relationship. Communication is the most important thing."

Having literally Secreted their 40-year marriage into existence ("Six months before I met him, I had these recurring dreams about this person I was going to marry,") they make sure their union has remained front-and-center even as their entire existence has shifted. "Marriage is a priority for both of us. And that means that we act on that and refocus when we've lost sight of the ball," she said. If the surgeon could prescribe one piece of advice, it would be to place that bond above all else. "The bottom line is this: I would do anything for her. Climb any mountain, take any bullet—in the chest, too, by the way. I might do things that justifiably make her really angry at me, but I would never let anything block me from delivering my love to her," he swore. If you appreciate how valuable marriage is to your long-term happiness, he continued, "You will never let anyone touch it."

ABC News reporter Roberts isn't always one for chit-chat. "I don't like the check-in," she explaind. "If you're calling just to say, 'So, what's up?' no, I do not like that." Everyone's favorite TV weatherman, however, is a phone guy. And after years of chafing against his frequent calls, a pal proposed something that changed her stance. "One friend said to me, 'Did you ever think that maybe he just feels comfortable when he hears your voice, because that tells him that all is right in the world?'" she recounted. "And I thought, 'That's very sweet. I'd never thought about it in that way. And if it means something to him, then it should mean something to me.'"Now, she said, "I have learned to take a breath and say, 'Sweetie, I've got some stuff going on, but what's going on with you? Great. I'm glad to hear from you. Got to go. Talk to you later. Love you.' That makes all the difference in the world to him, and it doesn't kill me for two minutes to be nice and sweet." They celebrated their 29th anniversary in September 2024.

The building blocks for their nearly 30-year union began back in their newlywed days, when any fight—one involved the Riverdale actor throwing the talk show host's ring out the window—felt like it could be it. "Early in a marriage, it's easy to let little things become big things—whether it's financial strain or career strain or you have kids and you're sleep-deprived," espoused the LIVE With Kelly and Ryan star. "But Mark taught me to walk away and take a breath. That's when you figure out that it's not a marriage-defining moment."Some hard-earned wisdom, to be sure, but now the parents of three are reaping the benefits. "Anytime you see a couple who seems truly happy, you can bet they've gone through some crazy, crazy stuff together and they've survived," he stated. "That's something to be proud of."

She's an introvert, she said, "maybe a step away from being a straight-up loner"; he's the ultimate extrovert "the mayor of everywhere," as he put it. She's a touch messy; he's "a little OCD" noted the Oscar winner. But, wed since 2003, they've long since learned to let the other do their thing. That's the advice the How to Get Away With Murder lead said she gives to all her soon-to-be-wed friends. "Marriage does not start when you walk down the aisle," she shared. "Your marriage starts when you look over at a person who you love more than anything, and there's something about him—just one character trait that makes you say to yourself, 'Oh man, that's going to drive me crazy. I don't know if I can deal with this.' And then the next minute you say, 'But you know what? I love him.' That's when your marriage starts."

You don't reach the 50-year mark in any relationship by letting disagreements drag on. Any time there's a blowup, noted the Grace and Frankie star, "Usually, I'm the one who apologizes. It's not hard because I love her and can't bear for her to feel lonely for even five minutes." Even better is when she can avoid saying she's sorry to the writer altogether. Her top takeaway, she shared, "Remember, when you're angry at your partner and say something hurtful, you will be more angry at yourself later for having said hurtful things to the person you love. You'll feel angry twice. Not good for your blood pressure, and certainly not good for your relationship."

Few things are more on brand than former New York State Supreme Court judge Jerry declaring their decades-long union works because he usually lets the Judge Judy icon win. But for his bride it's more about knowing you're not always going to like the final verdict. Their 12-year marriage dissolved in 1990 when he couldn't be the caretaker she needed following her father's death. Yet, when they got back together one year later and quickly remarried, she had no delusions that he was suddenly going to be the type to run the household or take the lead on birthday plans. "Every relationship is different, but there is a common thread of unhappiness, and that unhappiness comes from trying to make another person different from who they are. You can try, but they're always going to resent it," she explained matter-of-factly. "I don't think you should marry anyone with the expectation of changing who they are."

The Lost alum would be, well, lost without his longtime love, who he married in 1993. As he explained to E! News in April 2025, "My wife—being patient as I traipse around the world, going from job to job—she's kept our family stable. She's been fantastic."

Calling her a "very patient woman," the actor said his wife and their two sons keeps him "humble no matter what's happening."

"They shape my values," he added. "It's great to have that perspective and North Star."

#757. It’s our duty to promote ourselves: even to other scientists. Am I wrong?

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Recently, I submitted my faculty file to be considered for promotion. I thought that being elected as a fellow at one of the most prestigious research institutes in my field — bioethics — would strengthen my case. But it seemed that no one I spoke to at my university had heard of the fellowship, and the value of it wasn’t recognized.

I had an epiphany: if others don’t see the value, that’s on me. I need to better communicate why my work matters, rather than assuming that it speaks for itself.

So I withdrew my file and will resubmit it when I have developed a stronger argument for the significance of the fellowship, and will gather support from senior colleagues on its merit. I know my work is valued outside my own university sphere; now I must make that case internally.

If we want our work to count towards career advancement, it’s up to us to show our peers why it matters.

Am I wrong? — Brandon Brown, public-health and biomedical-ethics specialist at the University of California, Riverside.

“I couldn’t disagree more. I think it’s a shame that scientists need to almost beg their peers to see the value of our work. Most of us invest huge amounts of time, effort and funding into what we do because we genuinely believe it matters. If you truly think your own work is irrelevant unless you can ‘sell it’ to others, then perhaps you’re in the wrong profession.” — Juliana Sanchez Alponti Millar, biologist at the University of York, UK.

“The balancing act of spending your time doing what you think is important and convincing others about the value is tricky and always there — this is a good example of how you need your colleagues and mentors to understand your motivations and the ‘big plan’.’’ — Russ Altman, bioengineer and geneticist at Stanford University in California.

“I completely agree with this. As scientists, we often assume our work will speak for itself, but communication and visibility matter a lot. Many of us also lack marketing and self-promotion skills, even though they can make a huge difference in these situations.” — Mariana Belén Galeano, biologist at the University of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

“The beauty of science is that the scientific process itself sorts out which research is useful. Scientists should do science, publish it and, rather than spend time campaigning for their work, go back and do more science.” — Metin Eren, anthropologist and archaeologist at Kent State University in Kent, Ohio.

“Researchers do need to make their case, but they shouldn’t have to do it alone. Universities must do their part, too: set clear paths to promotion, review progress regularly and make sure managers explain to their staff members how promotion works.” — Timothy Davis, volcanologist at the University of Bristol, UK.

“We are our own best advocates. It’s taken me some time to shed the modesty and be comfortable with promoting my own work and accolades, but a friend once told me ‘no one cares as much about your career as you do,” and that stuck. You have to show people why they should care.’ — Margaret Swift, ecologist at Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability and Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine in Ithaca, New York.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-02203-2

Responses have been edited for length and clarity.

#755. Nikocado Avocado Tearfully Details Plastic Surgery Complications

After Nikocado Avocado (real name Nicholas Perry) underwent a second vertical torsoplasty following his 250-pound weight loss, the mukbang YouTuber detailed the side effects from his procedure.

Two months after the YouTuber underwent a second vertical torsoplasty following his 250-pound weight loss journey in 2024, he shared insight into the medical complications he's faced in the surgery's aftermath.

"I'm suffering," the mukbanger (real name Nicholas Perry) wrote over a Nov. 19 YouTube Short of a nurse clearing his surgical drains. "I had to get emergency surgery, pulled out veins, pulled out scar tissue. I'm full of regret."

Since undergoing his surgery in September—in which excess skin and fat were removed from the sides of his torso—he admitted that he hasn't been able to properly rest.

"I haven't slept in weeks, actual f--king weeks," the 34-year-old said in a tearful confession in a Nov. 5 video. "I have never been in so much pain in my entire f--king life. This is not OK to be constantly in this condition. I'm in so much pain."

Perry—who rose to infamy for his extreme eating videos and over-the-top meltdowns—announced earlier this month that the surgery had "gone wrong" and left him in nonstop pain.

"I'm living a f--king nightmare," he wrote in a lengthy Nov. 1 Facebook post. "I'm going crazy, NOT because of the torsoplasty but BECAUSE OF THE COMPLICATIONS and the SHOOTING pain in my fingers like they're being lit in a Gasoline fire or being sliced off with swords!!!!!!"

"Each night I have dreams of my fingers being sawed off, I'm trapped in a fire, crushed by a car, stepped on, drilled into, etc.," he continued. "I can't even escape this pain in my dreams. I've never been so upset in my entire life, truly."

Perry said doctors initially suspected a nerve compression in his armpit had caused the numbness and pain. He subsequently underwent an additional surgery two weeks ago to remove any sutures, scar tissue and pockets of fluid that could be touching the nerve.

However, the pain has yet to subside, with him adding that he's experiencing weight gain again—which he fears could split the incision—as he struggles with everyday tasks.

"I'm in the same amount of pain today," he wrote. "I can't ride my bike, I'm too unstable to drive, I can't do normal things like unload the dishwasher, fold clothes or type on my phone without these horrible F--KING STABBING in my fingers."

The influencer also reflected on the toll the complications have had on his mental health.

"I feel so f--king alone, and I've never had to sit in this much pain in my entire life," he added. “Imagine having a really horrible toothache that radiates up to your SKULL…. It's so intense that your brain doesn't allow you to think about anything else other than that."

"OK, now multiply that x10 teeth," he continued. "THAT is the level of sheer CRUSHING levels of pain I'm having to go through. I really was hoping this would pass in a week or so, and I wouldn't even need to speak about it, but I'm desperate, crawling in desperation."

#753. From conceding seven to Hull heroics - how Tzolakis recovered to defy Brighton

McBurnie stoppage-time double earns Hull win over 10-man Brighton

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic used one word to describe the performance of his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis in Sunday's 2-0 Premier League win against Brighton.

"Unbelievable," he told Match of the Day.

"Especially after the international break, which was very difficult for him."

Tzolakis' previous outing had been for Greece against the Netherlands in the Uefa Nations League, where he and his side were humbled 7-0 by the hosts in Amsterdam.

Nine days later, his contribution to the Tigers' first league victory since 29 August was every bit as important as that of striker Oli McBurnie, who netted both goals in second-half stoppage time against the second-placed Seagulls.

Tzolakis made a series of top saves to keep the highest scorers in the top flight at bay and, when Brighton full-back Costinha was sent off in the 89th minute for a second bookable offence, the hosts seized their opportunity to clinch only their third win following their Premier League return.

McBurnie said the 24-year-old stopper had "kept Hull in a few games" this season and the club were "lucky to have him", while Tzolakis told Sky Sports: "We are a unit and a team.

"We play for each other. We showed a good team effort and we deserved the three points."

McBurnie scores stoppage-time double as Hull stun Brighton

How 'outstanding' Tzolakis kept Brighton at bay

With the opportunity to move three points behind leaders Arsenal, Brighton looked most likely to score for long spells of Sunday's game, but just could not find a way past former Olympiacos goalkeeper Tzolakis, who joined Hull in August for a reported Â£20m fee.

He got down to make a vital block early on to deny Diego Gomez, who had slid in to meet a low cross from the left wing. It was the first of several occasions the Paraguay international would be frustrated in front of goal.

Tzolakis then raced out spreadeagled to foil Georginio Rutter with an outstretched left hand - a stop that BBC Radio 5 Live pundit and former striker Clinton Morrison described as "Peter Schmeichel-esque", referring to the legendary Denmark keeper.

Second-half efforts from distance by Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk were dealt with, too.

Yasin Ayari went close with a thumping strike against the bar and when Brighton substitute Charalampos Kostoulas pounced on a short backpass to go through one-on-one, Tzolakis got a hand on his Greece team-mate's shot and Regan Slater was back on the goalline to head the ball to safety.

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy, a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said: "We saw again how important Tzolakis is for Hull. He had one of those days where he was always in the right place at the right time.

"When you are a Hull player and you see the kind of saves Tzolakis made when he spread himself and kept it out with his foot, you start thinking that it could be your day.

"It happens a lot in football and, on the flip side, Brighton will have been thinking, 'are we ever going to score here?'."

Hull made a superb start to the campaign after being promoted via the Championship play-offs in May.

They followed victories against Manchester United and Coventry with a draw against Aston Villa - all without conceding a goal.

The Tigers had not won since that 1-0 success at Coventry until beating Brighton - but they are one of four top-flight sides still unbeaten at home and have not lost any fixture by more than a one-goal margin.

They lost 1-0 to champions Arsenal before the international break and Scotland forward McBurnie told Match of the Day: "We know we can make it difficult for the top teams in the league and we've proved that in the past two games.

"We want to make it as difficult as we can for teams to come here and make the MKM Stadium a tough place to come. It's proving that way so far, so long may it continue."

#752. Jamie Lee Curtis Details Being “Only Surviving” Member of her Family

Less than a year after Jamie Lee Curtis’ sister Kelly Lee Curtis died, the Freaky Friday actress detailed the grief surrounding her birthday as the only living member of her family.

Jamie Lee Curtis was honest about her birthday blues.

As the Freaky Friday actress celebrated her 68th birthday Nov. 22, she reflected on the death of her sister Kelly Lee Curtis earlier this year, which made her the only living member of her nuclear family.

“The long and winding road,” Curtis wrote in a post on Instagram. “Another circle around the sun! Today will be the first year, that I am the only surviving family member of my immediate family and my immediate second family. The last in the line. The loss of my sister Kelly in June was a real blow and I feel sad today.”

Still, Curtis—whose mom Janet Leigh died in 2004, while her father Tony Curtis died in 2010—emphasized the gratitude she has for her life.

“I look back at photographs of me as a child, and I look so stunned to be here at birth, and it carried on through much of my young life, always seemingly startled and slightly concerned,” she continued. “I've worked through a lot of that discomfort, and I'm so happy to be here and have the life I have. Both personal and creative.”

Meanwhile, Curtis—mom to Annie, 39, and Ruby, 30, with husband Christopher Guest—expressed desire to pass down what she learned from her late loved ones on to her living family members. “What remains for me is the legacy of other humans who forged a path for me to be here through their actions and examples as I hope I am for my own family and of course friends,” the Halloween star continued, “and, as a public person, the millions of people I've involved in my life.”

And, of course, Curtis knows she is surrounded by love.

“My husband and my daughters and their families and my young grandson, all of whom I get to see today for this life that I love so very much,” the Oscar winner continued. “I wish you all a happy and healthy Thanksgiving and holiday season.”

For a deeper look into Curtis’ candidness, keep reading…

Amid the chatter surrounding Pamela Anderson and Liam Neeson’s rumored romance, Jamie Lee Curtis quickly shut down any of the Naked Gun stars’ possible detractors.

“With all due respect to pop culture, if love has found [its] way into that relationship—God bless them both—leave them the f--k alone,” the Everything Everywhere All At Once actress told VT in August 2025. “Let them like each other. Both of them have had hardship, and they’re both beautiful human beings.”

And she further took a moment to heap praise on her Last Showgirl costar Anderson.

“She’s a beautiful person,” Curtis added, “She was fantastic [in the movie], but she’s a beautiful human being.”

The actress—daughter to the late Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh—hasn’t held back when it comes to sharing how seeing her parents’ later careers has shaped how she views longevity in Hollywood, and why it makes her more intentional about what she takes on.

“I have been prepping to get out, so that I don’t have to suffer the same was as my family did,” Curtis opened up to The Guardian in a July 2025 interview. “I want to leave the party before I’m no longer invited. I witnessed my parents lose the very thing that gave them their fame and their life and their livelihood, when the industry rejected them at a certain age.”

And she doesn’t want to be hurt in the same way. “I watched them reach incredible success and then have it slowly erode to where it was gone,” she continued. “And that’s very painful.”

As for her decades long career, Curtis considers herself an “old lady” jokingly adding, “I’m going to die soon.”

She takes bedtime seriously—and that’s why she doesn’t want to go to a concert in the evening. In fact, she has a proposition for singers.

“I’m challenging musicians to do concerts during the day,” Curtis posited on Today in March. “Why are there no matinees? For instance, I love Coldplay, I would love to go see Coldplay. I would love it, but the problem is I am not going to see Coldplay if they start their show at nine and there is an opening act. I want to hear Coldplay at 1 p.m.”

As for how the Academy Award winner wants to turn this dream into a reality?

“I think if we filled a stadium of people who want to see a matinee of Coldplay,” she continued, “I think we’re going to start a trend.”

The Freaky Friday star proved she was a true Californian by leaving film’s biggest night early to satiate her fast-food craving at the beloved West Coast joint.

“FLY IN [check emoji],” Curtis posted on Instagram March 2024 with a photo featuring her getting a meal at In-and-Out, “GET FLUFFED AND FOLDED [check emoji] PRESENT AT OSCARS [check emoji] GO TO @inandout_burger [check emoji] FLY AWAY.”

Walking Back Her Not-So Marvelous Take on Superhero Movies

After not holding back by saying a more recent phase of Marvel Cinematic Universe was “bad,” the Knives Out actress subsequently admitted she regretted her comments on the superhero movie franchise.

“My comments about Marvel were stupid and I will do better,” Curtis, who had previously shaded the Doctor Strange movies while promoting her own multiverse movie Everything Everywhere All at Once, wrote on X in August 2024.“I’ve reached out to Kevin Feige and will no longer play in that mud slinging sandbox of competition we call the internet nor will I engage in the toilet paper promotion or game play that is designed for clicks not content or conversation.”

For Curtis, a negative comment from a cinematographer while filming the 1985 movie Perfect alongside John Travolta resulted in an eye-opening experience with cosmetic procedures.

“He was like, ‘Yeah I’m not shooting her today. Her eyes are baggy,” she said on 60 minutes in May. “I was 25. For him to say that was very embarrassing. So as soon as the movie finished, I ended up having some plastic surgery.”

“That’s just not what you want to do when you’re 25 or 26,” she continued, “I regretted it immediately and have sort of regretted it since.”

And it influenced the way she views cosmetic enhancements.

“I’ve become a really public advocate,” Curtis explained, “to say to women, ‘You’re gorgeous and you’re perfect the way you are,’ so,…oh yeah. It was not a good thing for me to do.”

#751. Dubai Darts Masters returns to PDC calendar in 2027

The World Series of Darts will return to Dubai for the 2027 season; the Dubai Darts Masters has not been played since 2017; Gary Anderson was the last player to win the title in Dubai; watch the World Championship live on Sky Sports

The World Series of Darts will return to Dubai in 2027, with the Dubai Darts Masters set to be played for the first time in 10 years.

Dubai was one of the tour's original destinations and had previously hosted a World Series event between 2013 and 2017.

The World Series will kick off its 2027 season in Bahrain on January 15, before heading to the United Arab Emirates for the Dubai Darts Masters.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The tournament will see eight of the world's top PDC players battle it out in a 16-player knockout event between January 22 and 23 at the Coca-Cola Arena.

Scotland's Gary Anderson successfully defended his Dubai Darts Masters title when it was last held in 2017, beating Michael van Gerwen 11-7 in the final.

PDC chief executive Matt Porter said: "We're delighted to be taking the World Series of Darts back to Dubai.

"The city has a great history with the series, and Coca-Cola Arena will provide a brilliant setting for two days of top-class darts.

"We're looking forward to welcoming the world's best players and fans from across the region."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Eight first-round matches will be played on the opening night, before the knockout stages and the final are played on day two.

World Series ranking points will be up for grabs, as players look to secure their spots at the season-ending Finals in Amsterdam.

Ross Smith is out to defend his title after he thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals champion in September, winning his second PDC major.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Championship (December 11-January 3) live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

#750. Three years on NI Women finally have friendlies again

Northern Ireland's friendly double-header against Greece will be live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website

Tuesday, 18 July 2023 was the last time Northern Ireland Women played a friendly.

Under interim manager Gail Redmond, NI produced a fine display to beat Czech Republic 2-0 in Opava.

Just over three and a half years later, Northern Ireland will have not one but two friendly fixtures, with Michael McArdle's side taking on Greece in an Inver Park double-header on 27 November and 1 December.

A lot has changed for NI since that last friendly, but, having two pressure-free games finally offers McArdle an opportunity to experiment with tactics and personnel as they take the first step towards building for Euro 2029 qualifying.

Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies

Greece were beaten by England in the first round of the World Cup play-offs

Only eight players who were in the squad for that friendly win are in the current crop over three years on.

Rebecca McKenna, Rebecca Holloway and Simone Magill started while Lauren Wade, Kerry Beattie and Joely Andrews came off the bench.

Fi Morgan and Chloe McCarron were unused substitutes.

Goalkeeper Lilie Woods made her debut, Marissa Callaghan captained the side and Sarah McFadden and Beattie scored the goals in a rare away win.

A month after that friendly victory, Tanya Oxtoby arrived to take over as Kenny Shiels' permanent successor.

She eventually left to take over at Newcastle United in November 2025 and all 26 of her games as NI manager were competitive fixtures.

The introduction of the Nations League and its close ties to Euro and World Cup qualification admittedly left little room in what is now a stacked international women's calendar for friendly games.

During Oxtoby's tenure, NI had two Nations League campaigns sandwiched between Euro 2025 qualifiers.

After falling to Iceland in their Nations League promotion/relegation play off last October, they opted against seeking any friendlies at the end of November as they looked for a successor to Oxtoby.

The competitive games kept coming and Kris Lindsay was then in interim charge of NI's first two 2027 World Cup qualifiers before McArdle took over in April for the four remaining group games and the subsequent first-round play-off defeat against Portugal.

With NI not involved in the second round of the World Cup play-offs while many others are in the upcoming window, McArdle has decided to get the squad together for two friendlies.

With such a young squad at his disposal and with McArdle still relatively new to the job, he is relishing the chance to have the players in camp for an extended period and for NI to test themselves against decent opposition.

"We don't want friendly games in this window, we want to be in the play-offs but we had planned for both [scenarios], this has been a long-term plan," he said.

"Greece I specifically selected because I knew we couldn't draw them in the Nations League as we're in the same pot, but also they're a strong nation who are progressing well and are close to ourselves in the rankings.

"They'll be a real test for us. It was very deliberate selection."

Northern Ireland suffered a 7-1 aggregate defeat in the first round World Cup play-off against Portugal

McArdle wants NI to be "more horrible to play against" and feels they will work on that in this camp as well as what they do when in possession to trouble opponents.

Greece, like Northern Ireland, exited the World Cup play-offs at the first round after an aggregate 8-1 defeat to England.

They had been in good form before back-to-back defeats by the Lionesses, winning five games this year as they topped Group C4 to seal promotion to League B.

"It gives us two games to try and win first and foremost because we need to develop the winning mentality, but also to test some things because a lot of the identity and how we play, after six competitive games, there is still work to do particularly in possession, we've not quite done that yet," McArdle continued.

"That identity that we never give up and are constantly going, that is the case for the group, but we have to improve the athleticism and the duels to bridge the gap to qualification to tournaments."

Qualifying for the 2029 Euros in Germany does not begin until 2028, but McArdle's side have a testing Nations League campaign to prepare for next year.

They have been drawn against Poland, Finland and Belarus and the Scot revealed that he is already planning ahead for potential friendly opponents for next year's November/December international window to maximise time spent with his squad if they are not in the Nations League play-offs.

"There's also the importance of taking all the activity available to us and that's crucial for us growing and moving forward.

"We're already planning for next November/December window and selecting opponents because there is a deliberate strategy how we evolve the group.

"Part of that is strategically picking opponents which will help us grow. The friendlies, in a sense it's not competitive games, but we'll approach them in the same way."

#749. Jessica Biel, Justin Timberlake Share Rare Look Into 14-Year Marriage

In Justin Timberlake’s upcoming Apple TV documentary Timberlake, his wife of 14 years Jessica Biel shared some rare insight into their romance.

Jessica Biel is holding up a mirror to her romance with Justin Timberlake.

In the trailer for the *NSYNC alum’s new Apple TV documentary Timberlake, the 7th Heaven actress shared rare insight into their relationship.

“When I met him,” Biel—who first started dating Timberlake in 2007—explained in the new documentary trailer released Nov. 23, “he was just not what I thought at all.”

And while Biel and Timberlake—who share kids Silas, 11, and Phineas, 6—are notoriously private about their relationship, the Matchbox: The Movie actress admitted in a separate clip from the doc, out Dec. 11, “I think we gotta address some things.”

Footage in the documentary appears to confirm that Biel was referring to some of Timberlake’s public career blunders, including his 2024 DUI arrest amid his The Forget Tomorrow World Tour. (At the time, Timberlake took a plea deal, pleading guilty to a non-criminal traffic violation of driving while impaired and agreed to pay a minimal fine in addition to 40 hours of community service.)

Meanwhile, Timberlake owned up to his past mistakes, highlighting that he can’t stop the feeling of gratitude for his nearly 15-year marriage with Biel.

“She’s the best thing that ever happened to me,” Timberlake said. “That’s one thing that I did right.”

And the Grammy winner previously shared that Biel proved she was his mirror from the first moment he laid eyes on her.

"When I met Jess, it was undeniable how beautiful she is," the musician wrote in his 2018 memoir Hindsight & All the Things I Can't See in Front of Me. "I made some sort of sarcastic comment, really dry. Nobody got it except her. She laughed, and I noticed, all of a sudden, and in the way where you wonder if a person's like you, if they have a very dry, dark sense of humor, too.”

Although the pair had a winding road of romance ahead of them—they dated from 2007 to 2011 before splitting briefly and went on to tie the knot in 2012—Timberlake thought even then that when it came to Biel’s choice for a husband, “It’s gonna be me.”

“Thoughts kept leaping into my mind: I'm kind of really interested in that girl,” he mused. “There was just something about that girl.”

For a deeper look into Timberlake and Biel’s sweetest moments, keep reading…

See, all Jessical Biel wants Justin Timberlake to do is be her love.

"Happy Father’s Day to my spectacular husband who is one incredible dad," she wrote in a June 2025 Instagram of the father to sons Silas and Phineas. "And to all the other dads out there doing their thing. Leading with humility and vulnerability. Showin up with understanding and compassion, and always using humor to get through the hard stuff. Major respect and love to all y’all."

It appeared Silas and Phineas had that sunshine in their pockets, got that good soul in their feet. Jessica gave her Instagram followers a peek at their "family summer vibes" in an August 2025 post.

"You’re so many things to so many people," the 7th Heaven star wrote in a message for the singer's 43rd birthday in June 2024. "But to us you are THE ROCK. The rock we climb on, we lean against. The rock that shades us from the sun. And when we recline on you, as we always do, hopefully our butts will keep you eternally grounded and warm. We LOVE YOU."

Justin and Jessica's sons rocked the singer's Forget Tomorrow World Tour merch when he kicked off the concert series in April 2024.

"They got candy? LEGO!" Justin joked of their 2018 Halloween looks.
